q: An older woman has a bleeding basal cell carcinoma that requires wound care. Which feature of the tumor’s course explains why treatment should be considered?
o: A tendency toward early metastatic spread during the course of the disease
A tendency toward local tissue destruction with ulceration and bleeding
A tendency toward spontaneous disappearance as the untreated lesion progresses over time
A tendency to preserve surrounding tissue despite progressive enlargement of the tumor
explanation:
**Basal cell carcinoma** can cause substantial local morbidity despite its rare metastasis. Hazzard describes untreated growth producing local destruction, ulceration, bleeding, and other complications; the existing bleeding in the stem is consistent with that local disease burden (p. 1458). "If left untreated, relentless growth can lead to extensive local destruction, ulceration, drainage, bleeding, infection, and disfigurement." (p. 1458).

**A. A tendency toward early metastatic spread during the course of the disease.** Wrong, metastasis is described as rare, so frequent early metastatic spread is not the feature explaining this presentation (p. 1458).
**B. A tendency toward local tissue destruction with ulceration and bleeding.** Correct, local destruction, ulceration, and bleeding are explicitly described consequences of untreated growth, matching the concern raised in the stem (p. 1458).
**C. A tendency toward spontaneous disappearance as the untreated lesion progresses over time.** Wrong, the source describes persistent growth with local complications if untreated, rather than a tendency toward disappearance (p. 1458).
**D. A tendency to preserve surrounding tissue despite progressive enlargement of the tumor.** Wrong, growth can be locally destructive and can invade nearby structures, so preservation of local tissue is not the expected pattern described (p. 1458).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1458.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: A 75-year-old man reports altered food taste, reduced appetite, and weight loss beginning after changes to several medications. His mood is stable, he eats with family, and oral examination reveals no problem. Which area of evaluation most directly addresses the timing and taste change?
o: Evaluate depression and its effects on appetite and food intake
Evaluate medication effects on food taste and appetite
Evaluate chewing difficulty and its effects on food intake
Evaluate mealtime isolation and its effects on food intake
explanation:
**Medication-related taste changes or anorexia** are recognized contributors to poor nutrition. Hazzard includes medication review alongside dental health, mood, and social factors; the recent medication changes make that domain the focus here by inference from the stem (p. 166). "addressing polypharmacy or medications that can contribute to changes in taste or anorexia" (p. 166).

**A. Evaluate depression and its effects on appetite and food intake.** Wrong, depression is a relevant nutritional consideration, but the stem reports stable mood and a temporal link to medication changes, so this is not the domain most directly supported here (p. 166; inference).
**B. Evaluate medication effects on food taste and appetite.** Correct, the timing and altered taste match the medication effects identified by the source, making medication review the targeted next domain of assessment (p. 166; inference).
**C. Evaluate chewing difficulty and its effects on food intake.** Wrong, dental health matters, but the normal oral examination and medication-related timing do not direct the assessment toward chewing difficulty (p. 166; inference).
**D. Evaluate mealtime isolation and its effects on food intake.** Wrong, the patient eats with family, so mealtime isolation does not account for the specific timing and taste change described (p. 166; inference).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 166.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 166,410

q: An 83-year-old man with advanced COPD, FEV1 30% predicted, coronary disease, and frailty with CFS 6 is hospitalized with pneumonia. After 48 hours of antibiotics, he remains on 4 L of oxygen with little improvement. He has no advance directive. His daughter asks the team to do everything. Which approach best begins a goals-of-care discussion?
o: Recommend a DNR order from the disease severity before exploring his values
Recommend comfort-focused care before establishing what outcomes he values
Explore what doing everything means to the patient and family
Defer discussion of values while continuing the current treatment plan
explanation:
**Doing everything needs clarification.** Hazzard recommends understanding what this request means and considering whether interventions advance the patient’s goals (p. 1103). "When the goal is to do “everything,” medical teams may want to better understand what this means to a patient and family." (p. 1103).

**A. Recommend a DNR order from the disease severity before exploring his values.** Wrong, a recommendation made before exploring values omits the source’s requirement to understand preferences (p. 1103).
**B. Recommend comfort-focused care before establishing what outcomes he values.** Wrong, the source says recommendations should be based on the patient’s values and preferences, which have not yet been established (p. 1103).
**C. Explore what doing everything means to the patient and family.** Correct, this clarifies the meaning of the request before deciding which interventions fit the patient’s goals (p. 1103).
**D. Defer discussion of values while continuing the current treatment plan.** Wrong, postponement leaves the central request unexplored; the source recommends clarifying its meaning (p. 1103).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1103.

q: An 89-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia and osteoporosis develops agitation and pulls at his clothing. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, blood pressure 156/92, and heart rate 88. He has not passed urine for 12 hours, and bladder scan shows 850 mL. He takes donepezil, calcium, vitamin D, and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, started three days ago for urinary frequency. Which plan addresses both retention and the suspected medication contribution?
o: Drain the bladder and continue the newly started oxybutynin.
Drain the bladder by catheterization and stop the oxybutynin.
Start tamsulosin and observe without draining the bladder.
Arrange abdominal imaging and observe without draining the bladder.
explanation:
**Acute urinary retention** requires mechanical drainage, and anticholinergic drugs can precipitate it (p. 715). Hazzard describes “acute urinary retention that is precipitated (use of an anticholinergic drug, recent instrumentation, or alpha agonist drug)” (p. 715). In this vignette, drainage addresses retention and stopping the recently introduced antimuscarinic addresses a plausible contributor; the temporal attribution is a clinical inference, not proof.

**A. Drain the bladder and continue the newly started oxybutynin.** Wrong, drainage treats retention, but continuing the recently started anticholinergic leaves the suspected precipitating factor in place (p. 715; application).
**B. Drain the bladder by catheterization and stop the oxybutynin.** Correct, catheter drainage treats the retention and stopping oxybutynin addresses the plausible anticholinergic precipitant (p. 715; application).
**C. Start tamsulosin and observe without draining the bladder.** Wrong, medication and observation without drainage do not address the complete acute retention for which the source describes mechanical drainage (p. 715).
**D. Arrange abdominal imaging and observe without draining the bladder.** Wrong, imaging does not provide the mechanical drainage required for the acute retention described (p. 715; application).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 715.

q: An older woman with osteoarthritis develops a warm, swollen knee. Arthrocentesis yields 45,000 white blood cells/mm3 and no crystals. Which interpretation follows from Hazzard?
o: The finding fits the usual synovial fluid pattern of osteoarthritis
The finding supports attributing pain to cartilage wear without further evaluation
The finding calls for evaluation for inflammatory or infectious arthritis
The finding confirms crystal arthritis despite the absence of observed crystals
explanation:
**Synovial fluid leukocytosis** above 2000 cells/mm3 suggests an inflammatory or infectious arthritis etiology in Hazzard. OA fluid often has fewer than 2000 cells/mm3; applying that distinction to the stated count supports further evaluation rather than attribution to OA alone (p. 783). "Counts that are greater than 2000 cells/mm3 suggest an inflammatory or infectious arthritis etiology." (p. 783).

**A. The finding fits the usual synovial fluid pattern of osteoarthritis.** Wrong, the stated count is above the range commonly described for OA fluid and falls on the inflammatory or infectious side of the source distinction (p. 783).
**B. The finding supports attributing pain to cartilage wear without further evaluation.** Wrong, the elevated count suggests inflammatory or infectious arthritis, so the prior OA diagnosis does not adequately account for this fluid finding (p. 783).
**C. The finding calls for evaluation for inflammatory or infectious arthritis.** Correct, the count is above the source threshold for considering an inflammatory or infectious etiology; evaluating those possibilities is the clinical application of that distinction (p. 783).
**D. The finding confirms crystal arthritis despite the absence of observed crystals.** Wrong, the source associates visible gout or pseudogout crystals with crystal arthritis; no crystals were observed here, so this finding does not confirm that diagnosis (p. 783).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 783.

q: חולה עם דמנציה שהוגדר נוטה למות סובל מקושי חדש באכילה בזמן מחלה חריפה. לא ידועה התנגדות קודמת להזנה, ורצונו לקבלה הובהר. לפי המלצות משרד הבריאות, מה מתאים לדיון ב-PEG בשלב החריף?
o: להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה בעקבות הקושי
להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה לפי דרישת המשפחה
לראות במצב החריף עילה להקדמת התקנת PEG
לדחות התקנת PEG ולברר את המצב הרפואי
explanation:
**החלטה על PEG** בחולה עם דמנציה הנוטה למות היא רפואית ואישית. ההמלצות שוללות התקנה בזמן מחלה חריפה ומאפשרות לדחות את ההחלטה תוך בירור המצב ובחינת דרכי הזנה אחרות לפי הצורך; אין כאן הרשאה להתעלם מרצון המטופל (עמ׳ 6).
"בכל מקרה אין להתקין PEG בחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות כשהוא במצב של מחלה חריפה" (עמ׳ 6).

**א. להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה בעקבות הקושי.** שגויה, ההמלצה מפורשת שאין להתקין PEG במצב החריף המתואר (עמ׳ 6).
**ב. להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה לפי דרישת המשפחה.** שגויה, דרישת משפחה אינה מבטלת את ההמלצה הרפואית לגבי מחלה חריפה (עמ׳ 6).
**ג. לראות במצב החריף עילה להקדמת התקנת PEG.** שגויה, המצב החריף מצדיק דחייה והערכה, ולא הקדמת ההתקנה (עמ׳ 6).
**ד. לדחות התקנת PEG ולברר את המצב הרפואי.** נכונה, זו הגישה התואמת את ההמלצה בזמן הבירור של המצב החריף (עמ׳ 6).

מקור: המלצות הוועדה הארצית: PEG בחולה עם קיהיון הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 6.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות

q: A 76-year-old woman treated for hypertension reports dizziness on standing. Which measurement principle is important before changing treatment?
o: Use seated blood pressure to assess the response to standing
Use a high office reading to justify intensifying medication
Obtain supine and standing readings to detect a postural decrease
Use diastolic blood pressure in place of standing measurements
explanation:
**Supine and standing blood pressure** readings identify a postural decrease. Hazzard notes that postural hypotension is associated with falls and may be exacerbated by almost all antihypertensive medication classes, making its identification relevant during treatment. (p. 1222)
"always obtain supine and upright standing readings to determine if there is evidence for an orthostatic or postural decrease in blood pressure." (p. 1222)
"The presence of postural hypotension is an important risk factor for falls and may be exacerbated by almost all antihypertensive medication classes." (p. 1222)

**A. Use seated blood pressure to assess the response to standing.** Wrong, a seated reading does not provide the supine-to-standing comparison required to assess the reported positional symptoms. (p. 1222)
**B. Use a high office reading to justify intensifying medication.** Wrong, a high office reading does not establish the standing response; the source calls for postural measurements throughout treatment. (p. 1222)
**C. Obtain supine and standing readings to detect a postural decrease.** Correct, these measurements directly implement the recommended assessment for a postural fall in pressure. (p. 1222)
**D. Use diastolic blood pressure in place of standing measurements.** Wrong, focusing on diastolic pressure does not replace the paired positional measurements needed to detect a postural decrease. (p. 1222)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1222.

q: A 79-year-old woman with Parkinson disease recently started oxycodone and has severe constipation. Rectal examination confirms a firm impacted stool mass. Which approach addresses the current impaction and prevention of recurrence?
o: Increase fiber and fluids and arrange regular scheduled toileting for ongoing prevention
Add an oral maintenance-dose laxative and monitor the frequency of subsequent stools
Reduce oxycodone and adjust pain treatment while monitoring subsequent bowel movements
Clear the rectal impaction, then establish a regimen to prevent recurrent constipation
explanation:
**Rectal impaction** requires clearance of the retained stool before relying on a preventive regimen. Hazzard states that "manual evacuation should be performed before inserting enemas or suppositories" for a firm, large rectal impaction (p. 1376). Its algorithm follows disimpaction with a bowel regimen to prevent recurrence (p. 1379, Figure 87-6).

**A. Increase fiber and fluids and arrange regular scheduled toileting for ongoing prevention.** Wrong, these preventive measures do not carry out the source's indicated clearance of a firm rectal impaction; the figure places them in the pathway without impaction (pp. 1376, 1379).
**B. Add an oral maintenance-dose laxative and monitor the frequency of subsequent stools.** Wrong, a maintenance regimen is needed after clearance, but this plan leaves the existing impacted mass unaddressed (pp. 1376, 1379).
**C. Reduce oxycodone and adjust pain treatment while monitoring subsequent bowel movements.** Wrong, removing a constipating drug is useful in the preventive pathway but does not substitute for clearing the mass already demonstrated on examination (pp. 1376, 1379).
**D. Clear the rectal impaction, then establish a regimen to prevent recurrent constipation.** Correct, this follows the sequence in the text and algorithm: clear the rectal impaction, then use an ongoing bowel regimen to prevent recurrence (pp. 1376, 1379).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1376, 1379.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.1374, 1378–1379, Figure 87-6

q: An 85-year-old man with fatigue and weakness is being evaluated for suspected adrenal insufficiency. Which distinction between primary and secondary adrenal insufficiency is described in Hazzard?
o: Secondary insufficiency typically causes mineralocorticoid deficiency because renin activity is suppressed.
Primary insufficiency typically causes both glucocorticoid deficiency and mineralocorticoid deficiency.
Primary insufficiency typically preserves aldosterone because the adrenal glands remain intact.
Secondary insufficiency typically preserves cortisol because the renin-angiotensin system remains active.
explanation:
**Primary adrenal insufficiency** from adrenal disease involves both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency (p. 1531). Secondary insufficiency from loss of normal ACTH secretion causes glucocorticoid deficiency, but usually preserves mineralocorticoid secretion because the **renin-angiotensin system** remains intact (p. 1531).
"they have both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency." (p. 1531).

**A. Secondary insufficiency typically causes mineralocorticoid deficiency because renin activity is suppressed.** Wrong, the renin-angiotensin system remains intact in secondary insufficiency, and mineralocorticoid deficiency is not typical (p. 1531).
**B. Primary insufficiency typically causes both glucocorticoid deficiency and mineralocorticoid deficiency.** Correct, the source attributes both hormone deficiencies to primary adrenal disease (p. 1531).
**C. Primary insufficiency typically preserves aldosterone because the adrenal glands remain intact.** Wrong, primary insufficiency is due to adrenal disease and includes mineralocorticoid deficiency; intact adrenal function and preserved aldosterone do not describe that distinction (p. 1531).
**D. Secondary insufficiency typically preserves cortisol because the renin-angiotensin system remains active.** Wrong, the intact renin-angiotensin system regulates aldosterone, while loss of ACTH causes glucocorticoid deficiency. It does not explain preservation of cortisol in secondary insufficiency (p. 1531).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1531.
ref: Hazzard Ch 97 — AGING OF THE ENDOCRINE SYSTEM AND NON-THYROID ENDOCRINE DISORDERS
chapterTitle: Aging of the Endocrine System and Non-Thyroid Endocrine Disorders

q: Erythropoietin treatment is being considered for a patient with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. Which combination is associated with a greater likelihood of benefit?
o: A high serum erythropoietin level and a high transfusion requirement
A low serum erythropoietin level and a low transfusion requirement
A high serum erythropoietin level and a low transfusion requirement
A low serum erythropoietin level and a high transfusion requirement
explanation:
**Erythropoietin** is used to try to reduce transfusion requirements in responding patients with myelodysplastic syndrome (p. 1485). Hazzard describes likely responders as having "lower risk IPSS-R scores, serum erythropoietin level less than 500 mU/mL, low transfusion requirement, and shorter interval between diagnosis and treatment" (p. 1485). The combination in question therefore concerns both endogenous erythropoietin level and transfusion requirement.

**A. A high serum erythropoietin level and a high transfusion requirement.** Wrong, neither characteristic matches the favorable profile: the source identifies a low serum erythropoietin level and low transfusion requirement in those most likely to benefit (p. 1485).
**B. A low serum erythropoietin level and a low transfusion requirement.** Correct, both characteristics match the profile associated with benefit in the source, alongside lower-risk disease (p. 1485).
**C. A high serum erythropoietin level and a low transfusion requirement.** Wrong, the low transfusion requirement fits, but the high erythropoietin level does not match the favorable serum-level characteristic (p. 1485).
**D. A low serum erythropoietin level and a high transfusion requirement.** Wrong, the low erythropoietin level fits, but a high transfusion requirement does not match the favorable low requirement described (p. 1485).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1485.
ref: Hazzard Ch 95 — HEMATOLOGIC MALIGNANCIES (LEUKEMIA/LYMPHOMA) AND PLASMA CELL DISORDERS

q: A 77-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia is minimally responsive on morning rounds. Her core temperature is 31°C, blood pressure 85/50 mm Hg, and heart rate 45 beats/min. She was last seen well at the 22:00 medication round. Her medications are quetiapine 100 mg twice daily, mirtazapine 30 mg at bedtime, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and docusate. Initial glucose is 110 mg/dL. The ECG shows sinus bradycardia with J waves. Rewarming has begun. Which test does Hazzard explicitly identify as mandatory in the diagnostic assessment of hypothermia?
o: Serum thyroid stimulating hormone
Paired peripheral blood cultures
Noncontrast head computed tomography
Morning serum cortisol concentration
explanation:
**TSH measurement** is mandatory because severe hypothyroidism may underlie hypothermia. The source also lists severe sepsis, medications, and hypothalamic injury as potentially reversible contributors; this recommendation does not rank those causes below hypothyroidism. (p. 583)
"individuals who present with hypothermia may have underlying severe hypothyroidism" (p. 583)
"as a cause of the hypothermia, so thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) measurement is mandatory." (p. 583)

**A. Serum thyroid stimulating hormone.** Correct, the source explicitly requires this measurement to assess severe hypothyroidism as a cause of hypothermia. (p. 583)
**B. Paired peripheral blood cultures.** Wrong, severe sepsis is a listed contributor, but blood cultures do not fulfill the quoted requirement for TSH measurement; the source does not justify dismissing sepsis in this patient. (p. 583)
**C. Noncontrast head computed tomography.** Wrong, hypothalamic injury is a listed contributor, but head imaging does not fulfill the quoted requirement for TSH measurement; the stem provides no source-based reason to rank imaging as the mandatory test asked for. (p. 583)
**D. Morning serum cortisol concentration.** Wrong, the mandatory measurement named in this passage is TSH for severe hypothyroidism, not cortisol; the passage does not establish a comparative likelihood of thyroid and adrenal disease. (p. 583)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 583.

q: An 81-year-old man is hospitalized with a complicated urinary tract infection, fever, flank pain, and hypotension. Why should nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin not be selected for this infection?
o: Inadequate penetration into renal tissue for treating complicated urinary infection.
Insufficient antibacterial activity within the bladder during acute simple cystitis.
Limited activity against multidrug-resistant isolates, particularly in the case of fosfomycin.
Excessive penetration into renal tissue, making these drugs unsuitable for older patients.
explanation:
**Complicated urinary tract infection** extends beyond the bladder and includes pyelonephritis (p. 1711). Hazzard advises against nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin for complicated infection because of **inadequate renal penetration**, despite their roles in acute simple cystitis (pp. 1708, 1711).
"Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin should not be used for complicated UTI because of inadequate renal penetration." (p. 1711).

**A. Inadequate penetration into renal tissue for treating complicated urinary infection.** Correct, inadequate renal penetration is the explicit reason given for avoiding these drugs in complicated urinary infection (p. 1711).
**B. Insufficient antibacterial activity within the bladder during acute simple cystitis.** Wrong, the source includes nitrofurantoin as first-line treatment and fosfomycin as an alternative for simple cystitis. The problem here is penetration for infection beyond the bladder (pp. 1708, 1711).
**C. Limited activity against multidrug-resistant isolates, particularly in the case of fosfomycin.** Wrong, the source states that fosfomycin retains activity against many multidrug-resistant isolates. That activity does not overcome its inadequate renal penetration in complicated infection (pp. 1708, 1711).
**D. Excessive penetration into renal tissue, making these drugs unsuitable for older patients.** Wrong, the stated limitation is inadequate renal penetration, not excessive renal tissue exposure; the proposed mechanism does not explain the source recommendation (p. 1711).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1708, 1711.

q: איזה מהבאים נכון בנוגע לסמכות הרפואית הנדרשת להגדרת הסטטוס התפקודי המפורט במשפטים שלהלן?
o: מומחה ברפואה פנימית יכול לאשר סטטוס סיעודי מורכב וסטטוס סיעודי
גריאטר מחוזי צריך לאשר סטטוס סיעודי או תשוש נפש אם זקוקים ל"קוד"
סטטוס שיקומי מאושר רק על-ידי גריאטר
סטטוס מונשם כרוני מאושר על-ידי גריאטר או רופא ריאות
explanation:
## הסבר קצר

### הסמכות לצורך קוד:
במערכת הבריאות בישראל (קופות החולים ומשרד הבריאות), כאשר נדרש **"קוד"** (אישור לסיוע משרד הבריאות במימון אשפוז סיעודי או לתשושי נפש) (חוזר 26/2010, סעיף 3, עמ׳ 2), הגריאטר המחוזי הוא הסמכות המאשרת עבור סטטוס **"סיעודי"** או **"תשוש נפש"** – זהו הנוהל הרשמי הנדרש.

**א. מומחה ברפואה פנימית יכול לאשר סטטוס סיעודי מורכב וסטטוס סיעודי.** שגויה, טבלת הסמכויות מונה גריאטר להגדרת סיעודי מורכב וכן סיעודי שלא לצורך קוד. היא אינה מקנה סמכות זו למומחה בפנימית מעצם מומחיותו (עמ׳ 2).
**ב. גריאטר מחוזי צריך לאשר סטטוס סיעודי או תשוש נפש אם זקוקים ל"קוד".** נכונה, לצורך הזכאות הרפואית לקוד, הטבלה מונה במפורש גריאטר מחוזי מטעם משרד הבריאות כסמכות לקביעת סיעודי או תשוש נפש (עמ׳ 2).
**ג. סטטוס שיקומי מאושר רק על-ידי גריאטר.** שגויה, הנוהל מאפשר קביעת סטטוס שיקומי גם בידי מומחה בשיקום, ולכן ההגבלה לגריאטר בלבד שגויה (עמ׳ 2).
**ד. סטטוס מונשם כרוני מאושר על-ידי גריאטר או רופא ריאות.** שגויה, מונשם כרוני מוגדר בידי מומחה בטיפול נמרץ נשימתי או בריאות. גריאטר אינו חלופה המנויה בטבלה (עמ׳ 2).

מקור: חוזר 26/2010, עמ׳ 2, סעיף 3.
ref: קביעת מצב תפקודי (סטטוס) של חולה המאושפז בבית חולים כללי
chapterTitle: COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: The MIND at Home study found unmet care needs in nearly all community-dwelling dementia patients. Which care plan best follows the response Hazzard recommends?
o: Support safe surroundings, daily activities and physical and mental health
Support medical treatment while leaving home safety to a later crisis
Support physical care while setting aside meaningful daily activities
Support the patient directly while excluding the caregiver from planning
explanation:
**Unmet dementia-care needs** extend beyond medical treatment to safety, daily activities and caregiver support. Hazzard directs teams to "work with the patient and caregiver" and to "provide a safe environment that maximizes the patient’s physical and cognitive abilities". The point is to preserve function and dignity through coordinated support in everyday life, rather than respond only to a medical crisis (p. 924).

**A. Support safe surroundings, daily activities and physical and mental health.** Correct, this addresses the domains the chapter identifies and uses the patient and caregiver together to preserve abilities and dignity (p. 924).
**B. Support medical treatment while leaving home safety to a later crisis.** Wrong, home safety is an explicit care-team responsibility, so waiting for a crisis leaves one of the common unmet needs unaddressed (p. 924).
**C. Support physical care while setting aside meaningful daily activities.** Wrong, the recommended environment includes activities and socialization; removing meaningful activity leaves part of the care goal unmet (p. 924).
**D. Support the patient directly while excluding the caregiver from planning.** Wrong, the chapter explicitly includes the caregiver in the team response; excluding that person omits a partner whose needs and involvement also matter (p. 924).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 924.
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: An older adult has early gait impairment and backward falls suggesting progressive supranuclear palsy. Which eye-movement finding most specifically supports this diagnosis early in the disease?
o: Mild upward gaze limitation with preserved voluntary downward gaze
Preserved voluntary vertical gaze with no supranuclear ocular abnormality
Downward gaze palsy with an initially preserved oculocephalic reflex
Vertical gaze palsy requiring early loss of the oculocephalic reflex
explanation:
**Supranuclear vertical gaze palsy** is a key diagnostic feature of progressive supranuclear palsy. Hazzard states that "downward gaze palsy has greater specificity for PSP" and that the oculocephalic reflex is preserved early despite the voluntary gaze limitation. Mild vertical restriction can accompany aging, which explains why the direction and reflex pattern matter alongside the early falls (p. 992).

**A. Mild upward gaze limitation with preserved voluntary downward gaze.** Wrong, mild vertical gaze limitation can accompany normal aging; the chapter identifies downward palsy as more specific than an isolated mild upward limitation (p. 992).
**B. Preserved voluntary vertical gaze with no supranuclear ocular abnormality.** Wrong, this omits the vertical supranuclear abnormality that the chapter identifies as a critical diagnostic feature (p. 992).
**C. Downward gaze palsy with an initially preserved oculocephalic reflex.** Correct, this combines the more specific downward gaze deficit with the early preservation of reflex vertical movement described in PSP (p. 992).
**D. Vertical gaze palsy requiring early loss of the oculocephalic reflex.** Wrong, the source describes preservation, rather than required loss, of the vertical oculocephalic reflex early in the disease (p. 992).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 992.
